subject: Television & Streaming
title: CSI and the Forensic Fantasy
description: A 60-second lesson on CSI and the Forensic Fantasy.

hook.text: CSI launched in 2000 and made forensic science look like magic. Evidence always led to the truth within an hour.

buildup.text: The show used dramatic close-ups of DNA analysis, fingerprint scanning, and bullet trajectories in slow motion.

discovery.text: CSI created the 'CSI effect'—jurors began expecting forensic evidence in every trial, even minor ones.

twist.text: Real forensic work is slow, uncertain, and often inconclusive. CSI taught audiences a fantasy version of justice.

climax.text: The show spawned three spinoffs and a generation of crime shows that treated science as infallible and instant.

punchline.text: CSI made science look easy and justice look certain.

quiz.question: What is the 'CSI effect'?
options: Increased enrollment in forensic science programs
Jurors expecting forensic evidence in every trial due to the show
